title: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS): Plan Reading & Scan Types
realWorldScenario: A dashboard query filtering `orders` by `customer_id` and `status` takes 1.8 seconds in staging. The developer ran `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and asks you to interpret the output.
questionStatement: Analyze the four primary scan types in PostgreSQL: Sequential Scan, Index Scan, Index Only Scan, and Bitmap Index Scan. Under what exact conditions does the planner choose a Bitmap Index Scan over a normal Index Scan? What do `Buffers: shared hit, read, dirtied` signify?
expectedConcepts: Seq Scan vs Index Scan vs Index Only Scan vs Bitmap Index Scan
Bitmap Heap Scan reading physical pages in sequential order
Visibility map requirement for Index Only Scans
shared_buffers hit vs read vs dirtied
hints: Consider why random disk seeks are slower than sequential reads when fetching 5,000 scattered rows.
Check the role of the visibility map in index-only scans.
Buffers shared hit comes from PostgreSQL memory cache.
